instructions.purpose: Classify whether an incoming user message is a settings request or a normal conversational/task message. The result decides which handler processes the message: settings requests go to a dedicated settings loop, while normal messages go to the general assistant.

tool.name: define-settings-intent
tool.description: Returns an intent (`settings` or `normal`) with a short reason. Call this tool exactly once for every incoming user message before producing any other output.

instructions.language_note: The message to be classified may be in any language (e.g., Polish, English, Spanish). Classify based on semantic meaning and context regardless of the language used. Always provide the reason in English.

intent.name: settings
intent.criteria: - User wants to read, view, or display current assistant settings/configuration - User wants to change, set, update, or modify any of these settings: timezone, language, assistant name, address style, platform, preferred reply length, AI provider (openrouter / ollama / opencode-go), or the provider's chat model - User asks what timezone/language/platform/provider/model the assistant is currently using - User asks how the assistant should address them or refer to itself - Examples: "what timezone are you in?", "change my timezone to UTC", "call me Misiu", "use openrouter", "what model are you using?", "set your name to Bella", "reply shorter", "speak English", "jakiego używasz modelu?"

intent.name: normal
intent.criteria: - General conversation, questions, or task requests that are not about assistant configuration - Reminders, scheduling, memory recall, web search, web fetch, or anything requiring the general assistant tools - Examples: "remind me to drink water", "what did I say yesterday?", "search the web for X", "hello", "thanks", "explain quantum physics", "siema, co słychać?"

usage_rules.rule: Call this tool exactly once for every incoming message before producing any other output.

If the message asks to both change a setting AND perform a normal task (mixed intent), classify it as `settings`. The settings handler will apply the settings change and ask the user to resend the normal task separately. Never classify a mixed message as `normal`.

When unsure between settings and normal, prefer `normal` unless the message explicitly mentions a configuration concept (timezone, language, provider, model, assistant name, address style, platform, reply length).
Provide a concise reason in English.
The message may be in any language; classify based on semantic meaning, not keywords alone.

example.reason: Explicit request to modify the assistant's timezone setting.
User is asking about the current provider/model configuration.

example.message: "remind me to call mom at 5pm and also change your language to English"
example.reason: Mixed message containing both a scheduling task and a settings change. Per rules, mixed messages are classified as settings so the settings change is applied; the user will be asked to resend the reminder separately.

example.message: "remind me to drink water every hour"
example.reason: Scheduling request for the general assistant; no settings change.

example.message: "search the web for cheapest flights to Tokyo"
example.reason: Web search task for the general assistant; no settings change.
